idiom_name: protocol-conforming wrapper + lazy var / property wrappers / @dynamicMemberLookup
implementation_notes: Swift spreads the pattern across language features: `lazy var` defers construction of a stored property (virtual proxy) but is not thread-safe; a struct or class that stores the subject and conforms to its protocol is the explicit form; property wrappers package get/set interception into a reusable attribute; and @dynamicMemberLookup with a key-path subscript forwards unknown members in a type-safe way (SE-0252), which is the idiomatic dynamic proxy. @dynamicCallable covers callable subjects. The hand-written protocol wrapper stays the right choice when the proxy must be a concrete type with member-by-member control, when reference semantics are required for the stand-in, or when the subject is a struct whose mutation must be proxied (a struct wrapper then needs `mutating` forwarding or a class).
pitfalls: lazy var is not synchronized: concurrent first access can construct the subject twice - use a lock or an actor when the proxy is shared across threads.

A struct wrapper copies the subject reference on assignment, and mutating methods on the subject cannot be forwarded by a let-bound struct wrapper; choose class semantics when the proxy must mutate the subject.
String-based @dynamicMemberLookup defers every typo to runtime; prefer the KeyPath-based subscript (SE-0252) when the subject type is known.
Protocol extensions and default implementations may be statically dispatched, so wrapping a protocol existential does not intercept calls that bypass the witness table.
